headline_marked: No [[enforced disappearances or extrajudicial killings]] in last 6 months: Home Minister
headline: No enforced disappearances or extrajudicial killings in last 6 months: Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed claims no political persecution has occurred under the current government, while introducing a draft law to prevent future disappearances.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated on Saturday that no one has been subjected to enforced disappearance, extrajudicial killing, or political persecution since the current government took office six months ago.
Speaking at a panel discussion organized by Mayer Daak at the National Museum auditorium in Shahbagh, the minister addressed victims and families of past disappearances.

Addressing the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh, the minister claimed an independent investigation found no political motive, suggesting instead that Miraj may have been caught up in conflicts among robber groups in the Sundarbans.
The minister introduced the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act 2026, a draft law designed to ensure victims can approach courts for justice and redress.
The draft law includes definitions of disappearance, punishment procedures, and the death penalty as the maximum punishment for perpetrators.
It also provides for compensation for victims' families and ensures heirs receive property rights if a disappeared person does not return.

Human rights activist Nur Khan Liton challenged these claims, alleging that eyewitness accounts and digital data indicate law enforcement involvement in Miraj Sheikh's case and demanding a transparent probe.
The event was attended by several MPs, UN OHCHR Senior Officer Jahid Hossain, and family members of disappeared persons.
caption:
No enforced disappearances in the last six months, claims the Home Minister. But human rights activists are demanding more transparency.

Speaking at a panel discussion organized by Mayer Daak at the National Museum auditorium in Shahbagh, the minister addressed victims and families of past disappearances.

Addressing the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh, the minister claimed an independent investigation found no political motive, suggesting instead that Miraj may have been caught up in conflicts among robber groups in the Sundarbans.

The minister introduced the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act 2026, a draft law designed to ensure victims can approach courts for justice and redress.

The draft law includes definitions of disappearance, punishment procedures, and the death penalty as the maximum punishment for perpetrators.

It also provides for compensation for victims' families and ensures heirs receive property rights if a disappeared person does not return.

Human rights activist Nur Khan Liton challenged these claims, alleging that eyewitness accounts and digital data indicate law enforcement involvement in Miraj Sheikh's case and demanding a transparent probe.

headline_marked: Right-wing analyst [[Milo Yiannopoulous deported from US]] after staying illegally
headline: Right-wing analyst Milo Yiannopoulous deported from US after staying illegally
summary: The British political analyst, who advocated for the mass deportation of illegal immigrants, was himself deported to the UK after overstaying his visa.
details: British right-wing political analyst Milo Yiannopoulous was deported from the United States to the United Kingdom last Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed the deportation, describing Yiannopoulous as an 'illegal immigrant' who had been staying in the country without valid legal documentation.
According to US administration records, Yiannopoulous entered the US on a temporary visa in May 2019 but violated immigration laws by overstaying his visa and remaining in the country illegally.
He was arrested at New Orleans International Airport on August 27.
The irony of his deportation is highlighted by his own previous public statements, where he had advocated for the immediate deportation of anyone unable to provide valid legal papers.
Yiannopoulous was a strong supporter of the US immigration control system and had previously called for legal immunity for immigration officers while they performed their duties.

While he was a staunch supporter of Donald Trump during the 2016 election, he later became a sharp critic of the former president, claiming in March that Trump had 'lost his way' and was 'sold out to foreign interests'.
Despite his criticism of Trump personally, Yiannopoulous continued to support the far-right policies of the US administration.
